rows.question: i have [[Hardened Scales]] and [[Doubling Season]] and cast ballista for X=2. how many counters does it come in with? do i get to pick the order or is it timestamps
rows.expected_answer: You choose the order and the best answer is 6. Walking Ballista's 'enters with X +1/+1 counters' is a replacement effect (614.1c, 614.12), and Hardened Scales and Doubling Season are further replacement effects modifying the same event. When multiple replacement effects apply to the same event, the affected permanent's controller picks which applies first (616.1), and since none of the special priorities in 616.1a-d apply, any may be chosen (616.1e). Each effect applies only once to the event (614.5). Apply Scales first (2 -> 3), then Season doubles (3 -> 6). Timestamps are irrelevant for replacement effects; that is the layer system for continuous effects.

outcome.answer: **Walking Ballista** comes in with **6** counters if you apply **Hardened Scales** first (2 + 1 = 3, then doubled to 6), or **5** if **Doubling Season** goes first (2 doubled to 4, then +1 = 5). You choose the order, not timestamps. Under 616.1 the affected object's controller chooses which replacement effect applies, and under 616.1e any applicable one may be chosen. The ruling confirms you choose the order when two effects modify how many counters go on a creature you control, regardless of who controls the sources. Apply Hardened Scales first for 6.
citations: rule 616.1: "If two or more replacement and/or prevention effects are attempting to modify the way an event affects an object or player"
rule 616.1e: "Any of the applicable replacement and/or prevention effects may be chosen."

ruling a1f3da21-af6d-450e-bf0b-985d158418e6/636b245ed2960105: "If two or more effects attempt to modify how many counters would be put on a creature you control, you choose the order to apply those effects, no matter who controls the sources of those effects."
ruling 01546b7d-a233-4176-8843-d732074dc5b6/30e1af27509ea83b: "Doubling Season affects permanents that enter with counters."
oracle a1f3da21-af6d-450e-bf0b-985d158418e6#0: "If one or more +1/+1 counters would be put on a creature you control, that many plus one +1/+1 counters are put on it instead."
oracle 01546b7d-a233-4176-8843-d732074dc5b6#0: "If an effect would put one or more counters on a permanent you control, it puts twice that many of those counters on that permanent instead."

rows.question: opp cast [[Blood Moon]] while i have all three tron lands out. do i still get my 7 mana from urza's? can i tap tower for 3 colorless or is it just a Mountain now
rows.expected_answer: Tron is off. Blood Moon is a type-changing effect (layer 4, 613.1d) that sets each nonbasic land's subtype to Mountain. Per 305.7, a land whose subtype is set to a basic land type loses its old land types (so it is no longer an Urza's land), loses all abilities from its rules text (the colorless mana ability), and gains only '{T}: Add {R}'. Each Urza's land is a plain Mountain that taps for one red mana; Tower does not produce three because it no longer has that ability and the others no longer have the Urza's subtype. They are still nonbasic (305.8), so Blood Moon keeps affecting them.

outcome.answer: Neither. Once **Blood Moon** resolves, each Tron land is a Mountain that taps only for {R}. **Blood Moon**'s "Nonbasic lands are Mountains" is a type-changing effect, and a land whose subtype is set to a basic land type loses all abilities from its rules text, including the **Urza's Tower**, **Urza's Mine**, and **Urza's Power Plant** abilities. Each one keeps only the granted mana ability, so the three lands together give you {R}{R}{R}, not 7 mana. Urza's Tower can't tap for {C}{C}{C}. Per 305.7, the land "loses all abilities generated from its rules text, its old land types" and gains the Mountain mana ability instead. The Scryfall ruling confirms the lands "will lose any other land types and abilities they had" and gain "{T}: Add {R}."

rows.question: follow up: what if I play [[Urborg, Tomb of Yawgmoth]] AFTER the moon is already down? urborg has the later timestamp so shouldn't it make everything a Swamp too? my friend says no
rows.expected_answer: Your friend is right. Both effects are layer 4 type-changing effects (613.1d). Urborg's effect depends on Blood Moon's (613.8a): applying Blood Moon makes Urborg a Mountain and strips its rules-text ability (305.7), which removes the existence of Urborg's effect. When a dependency exists it overrides timestamps (613.8), so Blood Moon applies first no matter which entered later (613.8b). Urborg is just a Mountain with '{T}: Add {R}' and nothing becomes a Swamp. (Any actual basic Swamps you control are still Swamps because Blood Moon only affects nonbasic lands.)

outcome.answer: Your friend is right: Urborg's later timestamp doesn't make everything a Swamp. Blood Moon's effect and Urborg's Swamp effect are both type-changing effects in layer 4 (per 613.1d), but Urborg's effect depends on Blood Moon's. Blood Moon changes whether Urborg's ability exists at all, because a nonbasic land under Blood Moon loses its other land types and abilities, so Urborg no longer has the ability that makes each land a Swamp. Per 613.8a, an effect depends on another when applying the other would change the existence of the first. Dependency overrides timestamp (613.8), and a dependent effect waits until the effects it depends on have been applied (613.8b). So Blood Moon applies first, Urborg's ability is gone before it can apply, and no land becomes a Swamp. Lands are Mountains with only the tap-for-R ability, and Urborg itself is a Mountain with no abilities.

rule 613.8b: "An effect dependent on one or more other effects waits to apply until just after all of those effects have been applied."

rows.question: my goyf has two +1/+1 counters on it and I just giant growthed it. opponent [[Clone]]s it. is their clone a huge goyf too or just a regular one? and does the clone even know how big a goyf should be since the p/t is */*+1
rows.expected_answer: Just a regular Tarmogoyf. A copy acquires only the copiable values of the original (707.2): name, mana cost, types, rules text, printed P/T, etc. Counters, Giant Growth's +3/+3, and other non-copy effects are not copiable values, so the Clone gets none of them. The Clone does copy Tarmogoyf's rules text, and therefore its characteristic-defining ability (707.2a), so the Clone's own P/T is */*+1 computed from card types in graveyards (applied in layer 7a, 613.4a). The copy effect itself is applied in layer 1a (613.2a); your goyf's counters and pump are layer 7c (613.4c) and stay on your goyf only.

outcome.answer: The clone is a regular Goyf, not a big one. Clone copies only the copiable values of the printed card, which include the printed rules text and so Tarmogoyf's power/toughness ability, per 707.2. Counters and other effects such as Giant Growth are not copied, so the clone enters with no counters and without the +3/+3. Its size comes from its own copied ability, which counts the card types among cards in all graveyards and works in every zone, so the clone doesn't need to 'know' a size. It is just the current card-type count for power and that count plus 1 for toughness, the same as any Tarmogoyf would be right now.

rows.question: ok classic one. I have [[Humility]] out and my opponent drops [[Opalescence]]. what are Humility and Opalescence now?? are all my creatures still 1/1? does the answer change if Opalescence was out first?
rows.expected_answer: Walk the layers. Opalescence reads 'each OTHER non-Aura enchantment', so it never affects itself: Opalescence stays a noncreature enchantment and keeps its ability in every scenario. Layer 4 (613.1d): Opalescence makes Humility a 'creature' enchantment. Layer 6 (613.1f): Humility removes all abilities from every creature, including itself; per 613.6 an effect that has started applying keeps applying in later layers even though its source ability is gone. Layer 7b (613.4b): Humility's 'base P/T 1/1' and Opalescence's 'base P/T equal to mana value' both set Humility's P/T. Neither depends on the other under 613.8a (applying one doesn't change the text, existence, or targets of the other), so timestamp order decides (613.7). If Opalescence has the later timestamp: Humility is a 4/4 creature with no abilities. If Humility has the later timestamp: Humility is a 1/1 creature with no abilities. Either way every ordinary creature is a 1/1 with no abilities, and Opalescence is an unaffected noncreature enchantment. Any other non-Aura enchantment Opalescence animates follows Humility itself: its base power and toughness are its mana value when Opalescence is later, and 1/1 when Humility is.

outcome.answer: With Humility out first and Opalescence entering later, **Humility** is a 4/4 with no abilities, and it is not 1/1. **Opalescence** is not a creature (it is not an 'other' enchantment) and keeps its ability. Your creatures that were already creatures are 1/1 with no abilities. Enchantments that Opalescence animates also lose their abilities to Humility, but they are sized to their mana value because Opalescence's later layer 7b effect overrides Humility's 1/1. In layer 4 Opalescence makes Humility a creature (per 613.1d). In layer 6 Humility removes abilities from all creatures, including itself (per 613.1f). In layer 7b both effects set base P/T, and the effect with the later timestamp is applied last (per 613.4b and 613.7). Opalescence's static ability has its own timestamp (per 613.7a), which is later, so it wins. Humility's 1/1 still applies after it loses its ability (per 613.6). If Opalescence was out first, the timestamps flip. Humility's 1/1 applies last, so Humility is 1/1, and so are all creatures, including the animated enchantments, all with no abilities. The Scryfall rulings give the same two outcomes.

rows.question: quick one: if I have [[Valki, God of Lies]] in hand can I just cast the Tibalt side for 7? and while it's in my library/graveyard does it count as a planeswalker card for stuff like Vraska's Contempt / Kaya's Ghostform?
rows.expected_answer: Yes. Valki // Tibalt is a modal double-faced card: when you cast it you choose which face you're casting before it goes on the stack, and only that face is evaluated (712.11b, 712.11c), so you can cast Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor for {5}{B}{R} straight from your hand. Once chosen, the spell/permanent has only that face's characteristics (712.8f). But anywhere other than the stack or battlefield (hand, library, graveyard, exile) an MDFC has only its front face's characteristics (712.8a), so it is a legendary creature card named Valki, God of Lies there — never a planeswalker card.

outcome.answer: Yes. Tibalt, Cosmic Impostor is the back face of a modal double-faced card, so you choose which face to cast when you cast it from hand. Its {5}{B}{R} cost is 7 mana. You choose the face before it goes on the stack (712.11b), and only the face you chose is checked for castability (712.11c). Outside the battlefield and stack, though, the card has only its front face's characteristics (712.8a), so in your library or graveyard it is just Valki, a creature card, not a planeswalker card. Vraska's Contempt and Kaya's Ghostform only see permanents on the battlefield. Once Tibalt is on the battlefield, it is a planeswalker and both can interact with it.

rows.question: cast Stomp off my bonecrusher giant, it resolved and went to exile. my opp says I can only cast the creature half from exile now, not Stomp again, is that right? also can they counter Stomp with a 'counter target creature spell' effect since the card is a creature?
rows.expected_answer: Your opponent is right. When an Adventure spell resolves it is exiled instead of going to the graveyard, and you may cast the card from exile — but only as the creature (Bonecrusher Giant), not as Stomp again (715.3d). And no, Stomp can't be hit by 'counter target creature spell': while on the stack as an Adventure the spell has only its alternative characteristics (715.3a, 715.3b), so it is a red instant, not a creature spell. Everywhere else, including exile, the card is just the creature card Bonecrusher Giant (715.4).

outcome.answer: Your opponent is right about exile, and the counter idea doesn't work. Once Stomp resolved and was exiled instead of going to the graveyard, you can cast only the creature half, Bonecrusher Giant, from exile as a permanent spell, and only when its normal timing allows. Per 715.3d, the card 'can't be cast as an Adventure this way', so Stomp can't be cast again from exile. While Stomp is on the stack it has only its Adventure characteristics, which make it an instant, not a creature spell, so a 'counter target creature spell' effect can't target it (per 715.3b). Stomp is an instant spell while it is on the stack.

rows.question: my buddy says once I cast a spell he can't respond until I 'pass'. I cast Lightning Bolt at his bob, do I get to keep going and cast a second Bolt before he gets a chance to counter the first one?
rows.expected_answer: Your buddy is half right. After you cast a spell you receive priority again (117.3c), so you may cast the second Bolt immediately, before he can respond to the first. He only gets priority when you pass. Nothing resolves until all players pass in succession with the stack non-empty (117.4); then only the top object resolves, and the active player gets priority again after it resolves (117.3b). So he can still respond to either Bolt once you pass, but you are entitled to stack both first.

outcome.answer: Yes. Your buddy is right that he can't respond until you pass, but that doesn't stop you from casting a second **Lightning Bolt** right away. Casting a spell doesn't pass priority: you receive priority again afterward (117.3c), and an instant can be cast any time you have priority (117.1a). Your second Bolt goes on top of the first as a response, and it resolves first (117.7). Your buddy only gets priority once you pass (117.3d), so he can't cast a counterspell in between your two Bolts.

rows.question: I control a 2/2 with a Giant Growth resolving on it, and mid-resolution of a different spell it's technically at 0 toughness for a second (Maro-style hand-size thing). Does it die? And separately, if I have two Ragavan on the battlefield somehow, when exactly does the legend rule kick in - can I respond in between?
rows.expected_answer: 1) It doesn't die. State-based actions are only checked when a player would receive priority, not in the middle of a spell resolving (704.3, 704.4 - the CR's own Maro example). The creature only dies if it still has toughness 0 or less when SBAs are next checked (704.5f). 2) The legend rule (704.5j) is also a state-based action: the moment a player would get priority with two Ragavans you control, you choose one and the other goes to the graveyard. It doesn't use the stack and there is no window to respond between the second Ragavan entering and the legend rule applying; you can only respond before the second one enters/resolves.

outcome.answer: No, it doesn't die from being at 0 toughness mid-resolution, as long as its toughness is above 0 again before state-based actions are checked. State-based actions pay no attention to what happens during resolution (704.4), and they're checked when a player would next get priority (704.3). The Maro ruling says the same: a creature is put into the graveyard for 0 toughness only when state-based actions are checked. Giant Growth doesn't change that timing. On the legend rule, there's no window to respond. The legend rule (704.5j) is a state-based action, and state-based actions are dealt with before a player would receive priority (117.2d). So once the second Ragavan is on the battlefield, the next check makes you choose one to keep and sends the other to the graveyard before anyone can respond.

rows.question: two quick ones. 1) if I tap all my lands during my upkeep does that mana stick around so I can cast the mind sculptor in my main phase? 2) when I'm casting snappy can I tap lands in the middle of casting it or do I have to float the mana first?
rows.expected_answer: 1) No. Each player's mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase, so mana added during your upkeep is lost before your main phase (106.4). Tap the lands in your main phase instead. 2) Yes. Casting a spell includes a step where, if the total cost includes mana, you get a chance to activate mana abilities such as tapping lands (601.2g), and only then do you pay the total cost (601.2h). You do not need to float mana before announcing the spell.

outcome.answer: 1) No. Mana empties at the end of each step and phase, so mana you tap for during your upkeep is gone before your main phase. Per 106.4, "Each player’s mana pool empties at the end of each step and phase, and the player is said to lose this mana." You would need to tap for Mind Sculptor during the main phase itself. 2) You don't need to float mana first. Per 605.3a, a player may activate mana abilities "whenever they are casting a spell or activating an ability that requires a mana payment." So you can tap lands for Snapcaster's mana as the payment step arrives.

rows.question: i have [[Academy Manufactor]] and [[Shelob, Child of Ungoliant]] out. a creature my spider hit dies and shelob makes a token copy of it that's a food. with manufactor out do i get the food copy plus a clue and a treasure, or what happens?

The replaced event never happens (614.6): instead of the Food that would be a copy of the creature, you create one Clue, one Food and one Treasure token.
